name: DeepSeek-V4-Pro-0813
tagline: The heavyweight V4 finally goes GA — and it keeps Flash's MIT, LICENSE file and all
description: DeepSeek's flagship MoE reaches general availability as the 0813 build: the V4-Pro Preview architecture re-post-trained for agentic work, with the DSpark speculative-decoding module attached and a companion DSpark repo alongside. The card doesn't restate parameter counts for the GA build — the Preview's ~1.6T-total / 49B-active figures are the best public reference — and the safetensors shards total roughly 893GB, so 'Pro' means exactly what it says.
why: Two weeks ago V4-Flash walked DeepSeek off our fine-print-adjacent shelf; the open question was whether the heavyweight would follow. It does — MIT card tag plus a standalone 1.08 kB LICENSE file in the repo root, the same file Flash shipped. The agentic jump over Preview is the other story: 62.7 on DeepSWE against 12.8, 83.3 on CyberGym, 87.9 on Terminal-Bench 2.1, all self-published.
useCases: Frontier-class self-hosted agents where the API's terms or latency won't do
Long-horizon coding and terminal work at the top of the open-weights range
Post-training and speculative-decoding research on an ungated MIT frontier base
audience: Infra teams with serious multi-node hardware; everyone else via the API

setup.requirements: ~893GB of safetensors — plan on a multi-node FP8/FP4 deployment; unsloth and community quant repos are already carving it down

license.notes: Verified in the HF repo: standalone LICENSE file (1.08 kB, MIT text) in the repo root — the same clean setup V4-Flash-0731 established — with the card tagged MIT, the card stating repository and weights share it, and no acceptable-use rider or scale trigger found anywhere. DeepSeek-V3 remains partial in our catalog under the DeepSeek Model License; the V4 line has now dropped those riders twice in a row. Checked 2026-08-17.

tally.stars: 536 HF likes and ~22k downloads in the first days; unsloth mirror and DSpark companion repo live

limitations: Nearly a terabyte of weights puts self-hosting out of most orgs' reach, the GA card declines to restate parameter counts or context length, and the benchmark table is DeepSeek's own — independent evals were still landing at check time.
take: Flash was the promise; Pro is the proof. When a lab MITs its flagship — not just the efficient sibling — the license change is policy, not accident.
